### ① Premise and card fit
The card's Wanted 2 asks the two `workflow_run` triggers to stop starting runs their job `if:` skips. The readings comment measures 757 and 1,512 runs a day (mean over 2026-11-01..07) against 263 and 269 that can ever reach the `if:`. The diff is exactly one `branches:` line per trigger plus a comment block naming the card, the measured counts and the fact the trigger cannot see event or conclusion. Fits the card; no scope beyond it. The relay fold half (Wanted 1 action) is correctly filed off to `domain:skills` and not touched here: neither `fleet-write.yml` nor any sender is in the diff.

### ② The job guards are the authority, and they are unchanged
Byte-compared on `main` vs the head: the triage `if:` (`event == 'merge_group' && conclusion == 'failure'`) and the card `if:` (`event == 'schedule' && head_branch == 'main' && conclusion in (failure, timed_out)`) are identical. The narrowing is a strict subset filter in front of each guard: a run the new `branches:` drops is one the guard would have skipped, provided the branch premise in ③ holds. The card header's three-guard comment (card L111–122) still reads true after the change, because the guards it describes still exist and still decide. No stale statement found in either file's header.

### ③ Branch premise, per file
- `scheduled-full-run-card.yml`, `branches: [main]`: a `schedule` run of CI, Lint & Type Check or UI Coverage has `head_branch == main` (the guard already requires it), so every run the job can act on passes the filter. `pull_request` runs carry the PR head branch and `merge_group` runs the queue branch, so they are dropped, and `push` on `main` still arrives and is skipped by the guard as today. Sound on the documented semantics; the guard it fronts already asserts the same branch.
- `merge-queue-triage.yml`, `branches: ['gh-readonly-queue/**']`: every `merge_group` CI run has `head_branch` of the form `gh-readonly-queue/<base>/pr-<N>-<sha>` (the workflow's own `QUEUE_REF` at L241–255 relies on exactly this), and the seat read 181 of 181 merge_group runs on such branches on 11-07 with 0 runs of any other event there. The glob `**` matches across `/`. The residual the PR body states is real and correctly placed: whether GitHub's branch matcher applies to a `merge_group`-triggered run's `head_branch` the way the docs describe for `push`/`pull_request` is NOT MEASURED, and cannot be shown from a PR because `workflow_run` executes only from the default branch. The PR body names the post-landing check (the first red merge_group CI after landing must produce a Merge Queue Triage run and its comment) and the owner (the seat reverts that one line if it does not). That is the contract I hold the seat to; it is a recorded risk, not a finding, because the failure mode is a missing triage comment on a red queue build, which is the pre-#9424 silence this workflow exists to break, and the seat has bound itself to watch the first occurrence.

### ④ Tier and gates
Tier H (`.github/workflows/**` ×2): this record is the at-tier review; landing is by the maintainer's hand or an authorized approval, and the seat has said it posts the Tier H seat record and requests the governed approvers after PASS. Neither self-test reads the trigger's `branches:` (the triage harness reads the job's steps and permissions; the card's reads the `workflows:` line, concurrency group and crons), and `branches:` is on its own line below `types:`, so the `workflows:` regex is untouched; the seat reports both exit 0 at the head. `skip-changeset` is right for a `.github/**`-only diff. Clause-②: no, Metadata-protocol: none, both consistent with the diff. PR body `Fixes #31521` closes the card on a half whose other half is filed elsewhere; the card's own text records that split, so no objection.
